items.checks: Read all five mathematical modules and full task/reference/contracts. Native matrix coordinates and positivity bridge to the actual Euclidean operator. Full support identity yields cyclicity and exact subdifferential. Competing EReal potentials are proved finite from every supplied support; the two actual inequalities imply differentiability before equal-derivative uniqueness, with no hidden smoothness hypothesis.

The conjugate is the actual EReal supremum over all primal points. Positive definiteness derives injectivity and finite-dimensional surjectivity before building the inverse. Completing the square gives the unique optimizer, exact Fenchel gap/equality, actual dual derivative and both gradient inverse relations, retaining b in every formula.

Only semidefinite hypotheses occur in the singular branch. Orthogonal-kernel/image equality constructs an actual nonzero-pairing kernel witness outside the image; explicit multiples exceed every real bound. The finite value is independent of the chosen preimage; all optimizers form the full kernel coset, with uniqueness iff the actual kernel is zero. The scalar zero example is fully instantiated.

Read complete path-supremum construction. It uses the original continuous dual and arbitrary topological real vector space, without Hausdorff, norm, completeness or local convexity. All finite paths including the empty path are included, bottom is excluded, support values are finite, lower semicontinuity and real-epigraph convexity are proved, and minimality quantifies over every normalized supporting function.
The actual singleton record satisfies cyclicity. The same canonical potential is identically zero, and its (1,0) support is proved outside the input. No stronger equality conclusion is substituted.

Every finite subrecord containing the base is represented by the actual Finset index. Monotonicity and the supremum identity use actual finite paths. Finite slopes and cyclicity bound all path values, proving finiteness before taking toReal. Finite-dimensional convex continuity and the genuine directed-net Dini theorem establish uniform convergence on every compact set; no countable cofinality or unstated continuity is assumed.
